```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

candidate_roots <- c(".", "..")

project_root <- candidate_roots[
  vapply(
    candidate_roots,
    function(x) {
      dir.exists(file.path(x, "R")) &&
        dir.exists(file.path(x, "tables")) &&
        dir.exists(file.path(x, "figures")) &&
        dir.exists(file.path(x, "supplement")) &&
        dir.exists(file.path(x, "data", "pediatric", "processed"))
    },
    logical(1)
  )
][1]

if (length(project_root) == 0L || is.na(project_root)) {
  stop(
    "Could not locate the project root. Expected R/, tables/, figures/, ",
    "supplement/, and data/pediatric/processed/ either here or one level above."
  )
}

p <- function(...) file.path(project_root, ...)

required_pkgs <- c("readr", "dplyr", "tidyr", "knitr")
missing_pkgs <- required_pkgs[
  !vapply(required_pkgs, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]

if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0L) {
  stop("Missing package(s): ", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", "))
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(knitr)
})

require_file <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Required file is missing: ", path)
  path
}

read_csv_quiet <- function(path) {
  readr::read_csv(require_file(path), show_col_types = FALSE)
}

fmt <- function(x, digits = 3) {
  formatC(as.numeric(x), digits = digits, format = "f")
}

fmt_p <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  if (!is.finite(x)) return("NA")
  if (x < 0.001) return(format.pval(x, digits = 2, eps = 0.001))
  formatC(x, digits = 3, format = "f")
}

kable_clean <- function(x, digits = 3, caption = NULL) {
  knitr::kable(
    x,
    digits = digits,
    caption = caption,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
}

metric_value <- function(tbl, metric) {
  z <- tbl[tbl$metric == metric, "value", drop = TRUE]
  if (length(z) != 1L) stop("Expected one value for metric: ", metric)
  as.numeric(z[[1]])
}

# Core data objects produced by scripts 01-06.
X_raw <- as.matrix(
  readRDS(require_file(p("data", "pediatric", "processed", "pediatric_X_active_absorbance.rds")))
)
X_snv <- as.matrix(
  readRDS(require_file(p("data", "pediatric", "processed", "pediatric_X_snv.rds")))
)
wavenumbers <- as.numeric(
  readRDS(require_file(p("data", "pediatric", "processed", "pediatric_wavenumbers.rds")))
)
pca_baseline <- readRDS(
  require_file(p("data", "pediatric", "processed", "pediatric_PCA_baseline_3PC.rds"))
)
clusters_raw <- readRDS(
  require_file(p("data", "pediatric", "processed", "pediatric_clusters_baseline.rds"))
)
robustness <- readRDS(
  require_file(p("data", "pediatric", "processed", "cluster_robustness_objects.rds"))
)
sex_obj <- readRDS(
  require_file(p("data", "pediatric", "processed", "sex_sensitivity_objects.rds"))
)
strip_obj <- readRDS(
  require_file(p("data", "pediatric", "processed", "strip_reproducibility_objects.rds"))
)
transition_obj <- readRDS(
  require_file(p("data", "pediatric", "processed", "assignment_transition_objects.rds"))
)

# Publication outputs produced by script 07.
Table1 <- read_csv_quiet(p("tables", "Table1_pediatric_cohort_characteristics.csv"))
Table2 <- read_csv_quiet(p("tables", "Table2_exploratory_partition_stability.csv"))
Table3 <- read_csv_quiet(p("tables", "Table3_sex_and_substrate_sensitivity.csv"))
manifest <- read_csv_quiet(p("tables", "07_output_manifest.csv"))

S1 <- read_csv_quiet(p("supplement", "TableS1_cluster_stability_detailed.csv"))
S2 <- read_csv_quiet(p("supplement", "TableS2_PC1_PC3_sex_associations_BH.csv"))
S3 <- read_csv_quiet(p("supplement", "TableS3_clean_strip_technical_reproducibility.csv"))
S4 <- read_csv_quiet(p("supplement", "TableS4_clean_strip_direction_sensitivity.csv"))
S5 <- read_csv_quiet(p("supplement", "TableS5_participant_assignment_transitions.csv"))
S6 <- read_csv_quiet(p("supplement", "TableS6_pairwise_partition_agreement.csv"))
S7 <- read_csv_quiet(p("supplement", "TableS7_PCA_eigenvector_loadings_PC1_PC3.csv"))

clusters <- if (is.factor(clusters_raw)) {
  as.integer(as.character(clusters_raw))
} else {
  as.integer(clusters_raw)
}
names(clusters) <- names(clusters_raw)

if (!identical(dim(X_raw), c(25L, 793L))) stop("Unexpected raw matrix dimensions.")
if (!identical(dim(X_snv), c(25L, 793L))) stop("Unexpected SNV matrix dimensions.")
if (length(wavenumbers) != 793L) stop("Unexpected wavenumber count.")
if (nrow(S5) != 25L) stop("Unexpected participant-transition row count.")
if (nrow(S7) != 793L) stop("Unexpected loading-table row count.")
if (!all(as.logical(manifest$exists))) stop("The publication manifest contains missing files.")

pca_eig <- as.data.frame(pca_baseline$eig)
pc1_variance <- pca_eig[1, 2]
pc2_variance <- pca_eig[2, 2]
pc3_variance <- pca_eig[3, 2]
cumulative_3pc <- pca_eig[3, 3]
cluster_sizes <- as.integer(table(factor(clusters, levels = 1:3)))
baseline_silhouette <- mean(robustness$baseline_silhouette_by_participant$silhouette_width)

pc1_row <- sex_obj$pc_sex_results |>
  dplyr::filter(PC == "PC1")

sex_res <- sex_obj$sex_residualized_summary
strip_technical <- strip_obj$technical_summary
strip_primary <- strip_obj$primary_sensitivity_summary
pairwise_partitions <- transition_obj$pairwise_partition_summary
participant_changes <- transition_obj$participant_change_summary

strip_min_pearson <- metric_value(strip_technical, "Minimum pairwise Pearson")
strip_min_spearman <- metric_value(strip_technical, "Minimum pairwise Spearman")
strip_integrated_cv <- metric_value(strip_technical, "Integrated absorbance CV (%)")
strip_median_cv <- metric_value(strip_technical, "Median pointwise CV (%)")
strip_p95_cv <- metric_value(strip_technical, "95th percentile pointwise CV (%)")
strip_resid_ari <- metric_value(strip_primary, "ARI vs baseline")
strip_changed_n <- metric_value(strip_primary, "Participants changing aligned assignment")
strip_resid_silhouette <- metric_value(strip_primary, "Average silhouette")

sex_strip_ari <- pairwise_partitions$ARI[
  pairwise_partitions$comparison == "Sex-residualized vs Clean-strip-residualized"
]

change_lookup <- function(metric) {
  z <- participant_changes$value[participant_changes$metric == metric]
  if (length(z) != 1L) stop("Expected one participant-change value for: ", metric)
  as.integer(z[[1]])
}

n_change_sex <- change_lookup("Participants changing after sex residualization")
n_change_strip <- change_lookup("Participants changing after clean-strip residualization")
n_change_either <- change_lookup("Participants changing in either sensitivity analysis")
n_change_both <- change_lookup("Participants changing in both sensitivity analyses")
```

# 1. Scope and computational contract

This report documents the complete pediatric-only computational chain used for the reframed manuscript. It consumes the frozen outputs of scripts `01` through `07`; it does not fit an additional model, select a new partition, or introduce a new inferential branch.

The active matrix contains **`r nrow(X_snv)` participant-level spectra** and **`r ncol(X_snv)` retained spectral variables**. The report verifies the publication tables, figures, supplementary exports, and participant-level transition records generated by the analytical workflow.

```{r}
#| label: report-scope-checks
#| echo: false

kable_clean(
  scope_checks,
  caption = "Automated scope and completeness checks performed before report rendering."
)
```

```{r}
#| label: workflow-figure
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Pediatric-only exploratory analytical workflow."

knitr::include_graphics(require_file(p(main_figure_files[[1]])))
```

# 2. Data and preprocessing

The analysis uses the spectral windows **3400–2800 cm^-1^** and **1800–870 cm^-1^**. Three technical acquisitions were averaged before participant-level analysis. Row-wise standard normal variate normalization was applied, with no additional feature-wise scaling.

```{r}
#| label: cohort-table
#| echo: false

kable_clean(
  Table1,
  caption = "Pediatric cohort characteristics used in the active analysis."
)
```

```{r}
    "Maximum absolute SNV row mean",
    "Maximum absolute SNV row SD minus 1",
    "Wavenumber count"
  ),
  Value = c(
    paste(dim(X_raw), collapse = " x "),
    paste(dim(X_snv), collapse = " x "),
    format(max(abs(rowMeans(X_snv))), scientific = TRUE, digits = 4),
    format(max(abs(apply(X_snv, 1, stats::sd) - 1)), scientific = TRUE, digits = 4),
    as.character(length(wavenumbers))
  )
)

kable_clean(preprocessing_checks)
```

# 3. Spectral structure and baseline exploratory partition

PC1, PC2, and PC3 explain **`r fmt(pc1_variance, 2)`%**, **`r fmt(pc2_variance, 2)`%**, and **`r fmt(pc3_variance, 2)`%** of total spectral variance, respectively. Together they explain **`r fmt(cumulative_3pc, 2)`%**. The fixed three-PC representation yields exploratory groups of **`r paste(cluster_sizes, collapse = "/")`** participants.

The loading profiles retain the raw mathematical signs produced by PCA. No post hoc sign orientation is applied.

```{r}

#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Participant spectra, exploratory PCA score representation, and continuous PC1–PC3 eigenvector loading profiles."
```


## Continuous loading export

The full **793 × 3** loading matrix is exported as `supplement/TableS7_PCA_eigenvector_loadings_PC1_PC3.csv`. The table below lists the eight largest absolute loading coefficients on each component solely as a compact numerical audit of the continuous profiles.

```{r}
#| label: top-loading-audit

loading_top <- S7 |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(PC1, PC2, PC3),
    names_to = "PC",
    values_to = "loading"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(abs_loading = abs(loading)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(PC) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(abs_loading, n = 8, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(PC, dplyr::desc(abs_loading)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(PC, wavenumber, loading, abs_loading)

kable_clean(
  loading_top,
  digits = 6,
  caption = "Largest absolute loading coefficients for numerical verification only."
)
```

# 4. Partition selection and internal stability

The three-group solution is retained as a parsimonious descriptive representation rather than a uniquely established classification. Internal indices were evaluated for **k = 2–6**, and sensitivity to the retained PCA dimensionality was assessed for **2–7 components**.

```{r}

```

## Leave-one-out, repeated subsampling, and participant bootstrap

Across the 25 leave-one-out runs, mean ARI is **`r fmt(robustness$loo_summary$mean_ARI, 3)`**, median ARI is **`r fmt(robustness$loo_summary$median_ARI, 3)`**, and exact recovery occurs in **`r fmt(100 * robustness$loo_summary$proportion_ARI_1, 1)`%** of runs.

Across 1,000 repeated 80% subsamples, mean ARI is **`r fmt(robustness$subsampling_summary$mean_ARI, 3)`** and median ARI is **`r fmt(robustness$subsampling_summary$median_ARI, 3)`**. Mean pairwise consensus is **`r fmt(robustness$consensus_summary$mean_consensus[robustness$consensus_summary$baseline_same_cluster], 3)`** within baseline groups and **`r fmt(robustness$consensus_summary$mean_consensus[!robustness$consensus_summary$baseline_same_cluster], 3)`** between baseline groups.

Across 1,000 participant-bootstrap iterations, mean ARI is **`r fmt(robustness$bootstrap_summary$mean_ARI, 3)`**. Group-specific mean Jaccard similarities are **`r paste(fmt(robustness$bootstrap_jaccard_summary$mean_Jaccard, 3), collapse = ", ")`** for Groups 1–3.

```{r}
#| label: resampling-summary

resampling_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(
    Procedure = "Leave-one-out",
    Mean_ARI = robustness$loo_summary$mean_ARI,
    Median_ARI = robustness$loo_summary$median_ARI,
    Exact_recovery_percent = 100 * robustness$loo_summary$proportion_ARI_1
  ),
  tibble::tibble(
    Procedure = "Repeated 80% subsampling",
    Mean_ARI = robustness$subsampling_summary$mean_ARI,
    Median_ARI = robustness$subsampling_summary$median_ARI,
    Exact_recovery_percent = 100 * robustness$subsampling_summary$proportion_ARI_1
  ),
  tibble::tibble(
    Procedure = "Participant bootstrap",
    Mean_ARI = robustness$bootstrap_summary$mean_ARI,
    Median_ARI = robustness$bootstrap_summary$median_ARI,
    Exact_recovery_percent = 100 * robustness$bootstrap_summary$proportion_ARI_1
  )
)

kable_clean(resampling_summary, digits = 3)
```

# 5. Sex-associated spectral variation

Sex is associated with the baseline exploratory partition (Fisher p = **`r fmt_p(sex_obj$sex_cluster_association$fisher_p_value)`**; Cramer's V = **`r fmt(sex_obj$sex_cluster_association$cramers_v, 3)`**, 95% bootstrap interval **`r fmt(sex_obj$sex_cluster_association$cramers_v_ci_lower, 3)`–`r fmt(sex_obj$sex_cluster_association$cramers_v_ci_upper, 3)`**).

Among the three planned PC comparisons, PC1 shows the strongest sex-associated difference (raw p = **`r fmt_p(pc1_row$p_value_raw)`**; BH-adjusted p = **`r fmt_p(pc1_row$p_value_BH)`**; rank-biserial correlation = **`r fmt(pc1_row$rank_biserial_F_vs_M, 3)`**; Hedges g = **`r fmt(pc1_row$hedges_g_F_minus_M, 3)`**).

After feature-wise sex residualization, agreement with the baseline partition is **ARI = `r fmt(sex_res$ARI_vs_baseline, 3)`**. The aligned residualized group sizes are **`r sex_res$residualized_cluster_sizes`**, and **`r sex_res$participants_changing_aligned_assignment`** participants change aligned assignment.


# 6. Clean-strip technical reproducibility and sensitivity

The four independent unused strips show very high reproducibility: minimum pairwise Pearson r = **`r fmt(strip_min_pearson, 6)`**, minimum pairwise Spearman rho = **`r fmt(strip_min_spearman, 6)`**, integrated-absorbance CV = **`r fmt(strip_integrated_cv, 3)`%**, median pointwise CV = **`r fmt(strip_median_cv, 3)`%**, and 95th-percentile pointwise CV = **`r fmt(strip_p95_cv, 3)`%**.

Removing the direction defined by the mean of the four independent strips changes the exploratory partition to **ARI = `r fmt(strip_resid_ari, 3)`** relative to baseline; **`r as.integer(round(strip_changed_n))`** participants change aligned assignment. This procedure is treated as a sensitivity analysis, not as a corrected biological partition.

```{r}
#| label: clean-strip-figure
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Clean-strip reproducibility, supplementary projection, and sensitivity to removal of the independently defined strip-aligned direction."

knitr::include_graphics(require_file(p(main_figure_files[[5]])))
```

```{r}
#| label: clean-strip-tables

kable_clean(
  S3,
  digits = 6,
  caption = "Technical reproducibility of the four independent unused strips."
)

kable_clean(
  S4,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Sensitivity results obtained using each independently defined clean-strip direction."
)
```

# 7. Participant-level partition transitions

The participant-level comparison combines the baseline, sex-residualized, and clean-strip-residualized partitions after aligning numerical labels for display. Label alignment does not alter ARI.

After sex residualization, **`r n_change_sex`** participants change aligned assignment. After clean-strip-direction residualization, **`r n_change_strip`** change. In total, **`r n_change_either`** participants change in at least one sensitivity analysis, and **`r n_change_both`** change in both.

The sex-residualized and clean-strip-residualized partitions have pairwise **ARI = `r fmt(sex_strip_ari, 3)`**.

```{r}
#| label: transition-figure
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Participant-level transitions across the baseline, sex-residualized, and clean-strip-residualized exploratory partitions."

knitr::include_graphics(require_file(p(main_figure_files[[6]])))
```

```{r}
#| label: pairwise-partition-table
#| echo: false

  S6,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Pairwise agreement among the three exploratory partitions."
)
```

# 11. Reproducibility interpretation

The numerical results support five bounded conclusions:

1. The pediatric measurements contain structured multivariate spectral variation.
2. The three-group representation is useful descriptively but shows specification dependence and uneven group stability.
3. Sex-associated spectral variation contributes substantially to the baseline organization.
4. The unused strips are highly reproducible, while removal of an independently defined strip-aligned direction materially changes participant assignments.
5. The current design does not justify treating the exploratory groups as discrete biological or clinical entities.

```{r}
#| label: key-number-snapshot
#| echo: false

  key_numbers,
  digits = 6,
  caption = "Machine-readable numerical snapshot used for manuscript reconstruction."
)
```
